itemdesc-wingfabric: Linen sealed with wax or resin until it is taut and windproof. Stretched over the wing spars of a flying machine.
itemdesc-wingspar: Planks glued end to end with resin into one long, light beam. The backbone of a wing.
itemdesc-wing: A full wing: spar, stick ribs lashed with twine, and doped fabric stretched over it all. A biplane needs two.
itemdesc-cylinder-*: A finned cylinder hammered from two ingots. The ribs shed heat so the engine does not seize. An engine needs two.
itemdesc-crankshaft-*: A shaft forged from two ingots with a pair of throws bent opposite ways. It turns the pistons' push into the spin of a propeller.
itemdesc-engine: Two cylinders bolted over a crankshaft in a riveted iron crankcase, packed with rendered fat so it does not grind itself apart. The heart of a flying machine.
itemdesc-propeller: Four planks laminated with a jug of hot pitch glue and carved into two twisted blades. It bites the air the way an oar bites water.
itemdesc-chaindrive: Two gears salvaged from the ruins and a length of iron chain, greased so it runs smooth. Carries the engine's turn back to the propeller.
